title: The Wine Merchant's Son: Frankfurt, the Institute, and the Long Argument About Freedom
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: Frankfurt: The Only Child of the Wine Merchant

stops.name: Frankfurt am Main, born into an Orthodox house
stops.date_confidence: attested. Birth date and city confirmed by the International Erich Fromm Society chronology, the NYPL finding aid and English Wikipedia. The childhood address is given elsewhere as Liebigstrasse 27; no source reached in this pass confirms it, so the pin is Frankfurt city centre and not a house.
stops.campa: The only child of Naphtali Fromm, a wine merchant, and Rosa Fromm, born Krause, arrives on the twenty-third of March. The house keeps the Orthodox calendar. The family counts rabbis on both sides and carries the wine trade as a compromise with a world that does not pay scholars. They name him Erich Seligmann. He is born into one of the oldest Jewish communities in Germany, a community that has stood in this city for seven centuries and has thirty-three years left.
sources: International Erich Fromm Society chronology, fromm-online.org/en/life/important-dates/
suggested_refs: The Frankfurt Judengasse and Westend communities into which the Fromm and Krause families married

stops.name: Frankfurt, the last examination of the war
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year, defaulted to January for want of a month. The Fromm Society chronology and English Wikipedia both give 1918 for the final examination at the Woehler-Realgymnasium. Coordinates corrected: German Wikipedia places the school in the Lessingstrasse, Westend-Sued, from 1870 until the building was destroyed by air raid; the Dornbusch site dates only from May 1957.
stops.campa: He sits his final examination at the Woehler-Realgymnasium in the Lessingstrasse, in the Westend, in the last year of the war. Around the school a city has spent four years learning to hate on command, and the hatred lifts in November as suddenly as it arrived. He is eighteen and already asking what makes an ordinary man believe what the crowd around him requires. The Lessingstrasse building is destroyed by air raid in the next war, and the school reopens in Dornbusch in 1957.
sources: International Erich Fromm Society chronology, fromm-online.org/en/life/important-dates/
suggested_refs: The Woehlerschule's present site at Mierendorffstrasse 6, Dornbusch, occupied from 1957

stops.name: Bockenheim, two semesters of jurisprudence
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year, month set to the winter semester by convention and not by a document. Coordinates corrected to the Campus Bockenheim figures given by German Wikipedia; the research pool's pin sat some 750 m off campus.
stops.campa: He enrols at the University of Frankfurt on the Bockenheim campus and reads law. Two semesters are enough. Jurisprudence teaches the rules a society writes down, and what he wants to know is why people obey the ones nobody wrote. The Institut fuer Sozialforschung, whose social psychology he will run from 1930, is put up a few streets from this campus for a science that does not yet exist in 1918. He leaves for Heidelberg in the summer of 1919 and does not come back to the law faculty.
sources: International Erich Fromm Society chronology, fromm-online.org/en/life/important-dates/
suggested_refs: The Bockenheim campus of the Johann Wolfgang Goethe University, founded 1914

stops.name: Frankfurt, the Free Jewish House of Learning
stops.date_confidence: contested, and left contested. The Fromm Society chronology reads 1919 and calls him a co-founder. German Wikipedia dates the founding to 1920 under Franz Rosenzweig and does not mention Fromm anywhere in the article, as founder, teacher or participant. martin_buber.journey.json states that Fromm taught there alongside Buber. The German article also records that the Lehrhaus had no fixed address, so Boersenstrasse 7, a 1923 venue, cannot anchor this stop; the pin is inherited byte-identical from martin_buber.journey.json at Frankfurt city precision.
stops.campa: Franz Rosenzweig opens the Freies Juedisches Lehrhaus, a house of learning for adults who have lost their Hebrew and want it back. It has no fixed address and borrows rooms across the city. Martin Buber teaches there, and Gershom Scholem, and Leo Loewenthal, in a Judaism read as a living argument rather than an inheritance. Fromm's own society calls him a co-founder. The Lehrhaus's record does not name him at all, in any role. Whether he stood in the founding circle or only in the borrowed rooms is a question nothing reached answers.
sources: International Erich Fromm Society chronology, fromm-online.org/en/life/important-dates/
suggested_refs: Franz Rosenzweig's Lehrhaus programme and its borrowed rooms, including the Elisabethenschule at Boersenstrasse 7 in 1923

segments.name: Heidelberg: The Law, the Talmud, and the Cure

stops.name: Heidelberg, sociology in the morning and Talmud in the afternoon
stops.date_confidence: attested. English Wikipedia gives Heidelberg from summer 1919; the Fromm Society chronology dates the switch to sociology to 1920 and the Rabinkow study as running to 1925. Month set to the summer semester on that basis.
stops.campa: From the summer of 1919 he studies at Heidelberg, and within a year he has left law for sociology under Alfred Weber. Karl Jaspers lectures in this town, and Heinrich Rickert. Two educations run side by side and he never reconciles them. The German sociology of religion takes his mornings in the lecture hall. His afternoons go to a rented room where he sits with Salman Baruch Rabinkow, a Lithuanian Talmudist of the Chabad line, over an open page of the Gemara, almost daily until 1925.
sources: International Erich Fromm Society chronology, fromm-online.org/en/life/important-dates/
suggested_refs: Salman Baruch Rabinkow's Heidelberg room, where Fromm read Talmud from 1920 to 1925

stops.name: Heidelberg, the doctorate on a law without a country
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year by the Fromm Society chronology and English Wikipedia, both naming Alfred Weber as supervisor; no month recorded, defaulted to January.
stops.campa: Alfred Weber accepts the doctorate. Das juedische Gesetz is a sociology of diaspora Judaism, and it asks how a law with no state and no territory behind it holds a people together for two thousand years. His answer is that the law works as a social structure before it works as a faith, that it forms a character and the character carries the belief. The thesis is not published in his lifetime. The question inside it, how obedience is made, is the question of every book he writes afterwards. He is twenty-two.
sources: International Erich Fromm Society chronology, fromm-online.org/en/life/important-dates/
suggested_refs: Das juedische Gesetz: Ein Beitrag zur Soziologie des Diaspora-Judentums, Heidelberg dissertation, 1922

stops.name: Heidelberg-Neuenheim, the Therapeutikum on the Moenchhofstrasse
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year by the Fromm Society chronology, which names the Moenchhofstrasse and Frieda Reichmann; no month recorded. Coordinates corrected to the Neuenheim district centre given by German Wikipedia, the research pool's pin having fallen south of the district at the Neckar edge.
stops.campa: On the Moenchhofstrasse in Neuenheim, north of the Neckar, he opens a sanatorium with Frieda Reichmann, a physician and analyst ten years his senior. The house is psychoanalytic and Torah-observant at once. The observance falls away within a few years; the analysis does not. Fromm enters analysis here himself, with Reichmann, who is at that moment his doctor, his partner in the enterprise, and the woman he will marry. Patients are analysed in the morning and keep the dietary laws at table, and the circle jokes that the place is a Thorapeutikum.
stops.quote: Man's main task in life is to give birth to himself, to become what he potentially is.
stops.quote_source: Erich Fromm, Man for Himself (1947), Ch. 4, via Wikiquote's sourced-quotations compilation
sources: International Erich Fromm Society chronology, fromm-online.org/en/life/important-dates/
suggested_refs: The Therapeutikum at Heidelberg-Neuenheim, the only Torah-observant psychoanalytic sanatorium in Germany

stops.name: Heidelberg, the marriage to Frieda Reichmann
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by the Fromm Society chronology and English Wikipedia. The Baden-Baden contact with Georg Groddeck is dated 1926 by the Fromm Society chronology alone, at city precision with no building identified, and is folded into this stop rather than given a pin of its own.
stops.campa: On the sixteenth of June he marries Frieda Reichmann, who has been his analyst and is ten years his senior. They separate in 1931 when he falls ill, and they stay colleagues for the rest of her life; she will be among the founders of his New York institute nearly twenty years later. In these same months he travels to Baden-Baden to sit with Georg Groddeck, the heterodox physician who reads an organic illness as something the body is saying, and takes from him a lasting distrust of doctrine inside analysis.
stops.quote: In erotic love, two people who were separate become one. In motherly love, two people who were one become separate.
stops.quote_source: Erich Fromm, The Art of Loving (1956), Ch. 2, via Wikiquote's sourced-quotations compilation
sources: International Erich Fromm Society chronology, fromm-online.org/en/life/important-dates/
suggested_refs: Georg Groddeck's sanatorium practice at Baden-Baden and his Book of the It

segments.name: Berlin, Frankfurt, Davos: The Institute Years

stops.name: Berlin, the training analysis with Hanns Sachs
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year by the Fromm Society chronology, which places the didactic analysis with Hanns Sachs at the Berlin Psychoanalytic Institute in 1928 and the completion of training in 1930. The coordinate is an approximate historical Tiergarten-district location for the Institute, not a confirmed street address.
stops.campa: He goes to Berlin for the training the profession requires and takes his didactic analysis with Hanns Sachs, one of Freud's earliest and closest collaborators. The Berlin Psychoanalytic Institute is the most rigorous school in Europe and among the most orthodox. He is admitted to it in the same years in which he begins to doubt its doctrine of the drives. He finishes the training in 1930, qualified as a lay analyst with a doctorate in sociology and no medical degree, and publishing as a Freudian in good standing.
sources: International Erich Fromm Society chronology, fromm-online.org/en/life/important-dates/
suggested_refs: The Berlin Psychoanalytic Institute and its free polyclinic, model for psychoanalytic training between the wars

stops.name: Berlin, the practice at Bayerischer Platz
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of the practice by the Fromm Society chronology. The residence is attested by German Wikipedia, 'Bayerischer Platz': Am Bayerischen Platz 1 wohnte Erich Fromm. The plaque-series name reported by one automated summary could not be confirmed and is not asserted here.
stops.campa: He opens his own practice and lives at Bayerischer Platz 1 in Schoeneberg, in the quarter where much of the city's psychoanalytic profession keeps its consulting rooms. A plaque on the building records the address as his. Four years remain to him in Germany, and the decrees that will empty this quarter of its analysts are not yet written. In 1993 the square is hung with the Orte des Erinnerns signs, each printed with a single decree of the Nazi laws against the Jews of Berlin, one law to a sign.
sources: International Erich Fromm Society chronology, fromm-online.org/en/life/important-dates/
suggested_refs: The Orte des Erinnerns installation at Bayerischer Platz, Berlin-Schoeneberg, 1993

stops.name: Frankfurt, the Institute for Social Research
stops.date_confidence: attested. English Wikipedia and the Fromm Society chronology both date his entry to the Institut fuer Sozialforschung to 1930, under Horkheimer's directorship; the South German Institute for Psychoanalysis is dated 1929 by the same chronology and is folded in here for want of an address. Month set to order the segment. Pin inherited byte-identical from felix_weil.journey.json. Flagged: the Institute's 1924 Viktoria-Allee building actually stood at 50.1184, 8.6539, some 750 m west of this pin, and was bombed in the war and demolished in 1950.
stops.campa: Max Horkheimer takes over the Institut fuer Sozialforschung and brings Fromm in to run its social psychology, the psychoanalytic half of a synthesis of Marx and Freud that nobody has yet made work. The year before, Fromm had helped found the South German Institute for Psychoanalysis in the same city. The Institute's money is Hermann Weil's grain fortune, made shipping wheat out of Buenos Aires and settled on the school by his son Felix Weil. The salary of the century's most widely read psychoanalyst is paid, at one remove, by the Argentine pampa.
sources: International Erich Fromm Society chronology, fromm-online.org/en/life/important-dates/
suggested_refs: The Institute building on the Viktoria-Allee, today the Senckenberganlage, destroyed by bombing and demolished in 1950

stops.name: Davos, the Schatzalp above the valley
stops.date_confidence: attested for the illness and the years by the Fromm Society chronology, which records repeated stays from 1931 to 1934 and a further six-month convalescence in 1938; no month recorded for the first arrival. Coordinates confirmed against English Wikipedia, 'Schatzalp'.
stops.campa: Tuberculosis takes him to the Schatzalp above Davos, the south-facing sanatorium reached by funicular that furnished Thomas Mann the Berghof of his mountain novel. He separates from Frieda Reichmann. The two essays he publishes in 1932 in the Institute's journal set out his whole programme in advance: character is formed in the family, and the family is the belt that drives an economy into an ideology. He stays up on the mountain, on and off, until 1934, and comes back for six months in 1938.
stops.quote: Uncertainty is the very condition to impel man to unfold his powers.
stops.quote_source: Erich Fromm, Man for Himself (1947), Ch. 3, via Wikiquote's sourced-quotations compilation
sources: International Erich Fromm Society chronology, fromm-online.org/en/life/important-dates/
suggested_refs: Ueber Methode und Aufgaben einer analytischen Sozialpsychologie, Zeitschrift fuer Sozialforschung, 1932

stops.name: Chicago, the guest lectures and a death at home
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year by the Fromm Society chronology, which records both the Chicago guest lectures and the death of Naphtali Fromm in 1933. No source reached names the host institution, the lecture subjects, or the month; the pin is Chicago at city precision.
stops.campa: He crosses the Atlantic to lecture in Chicago, his first sight of the country that will hold him for forty years, in the year the Reichstag burns. The American audience hears a European Freudian who is already arguing with Freud. Naphtali Fromm dies in Germany the same year, and the wine merchant's son is thirty-three and out of the country when it happens. He goes back to a Frankfurt that is already emptying. Which institution invited him, and on what, is not recorded in anything reachable.
sources: International Erich Fromm Society chronology, fromm-online.org/en/life/important-dates/
suggested_refs: The Chicago psychoanalytic milieu of the early 1930s, host of many of the first European analysts to lecture in America

segments.name: Out Through Geneva: The Exiled School

stops.name: Geneva, the Institute in transit
stops.date_confidence: attested, after a correction. The research pool first recorded Geneva as an unconfirmed dossier lead; the verification pass found English Wikipedia's Fromm article states he moved to Geneva after the Nazi takeover and then to Columbia in 1934. Note that the Fromm Society chronology does not mention Geneva at all. Month set to order the segment.
stops.campa: The Institute moves its branch office to Geneva as Germany closes behind it, and Fromm goes with the move. The endowment, the journal, the staff: all of it has to be got out of a state that has begun stripping Jews of their posts by decree. The men who theorised the authoritarian character from a lecture hall will finish the argument as refugees. The journal will be printed in Paris and the school reassembled in New York. Geneva is a waiting room with a lake.
suggested_refs: The Institute's Geneva branch office and its Paris outpost at the Ecole normale superieure, from which the Zeitschrift was printed 1933-1939

stops.name: Columbia University, arrival on the thirty-first of May
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by the Fromm Society chronology, which gives the forced emigration as 25 May and the New York arrival as 31 May 1934. Pin inherited byte-identical from felix_weil.journey.json.
stops.campa: He is forced out of Germany on the twenty-fifth of May and lands in New York on the thirty-first, six days later, as the Institute reconstitutes itself on Morningside Heights under Columbia's roof. The exiled school keeps its German name and its German journal and behaves for a while as though the move were temporary. He is the only one of them who will learn to write English for Americans, and doing so will cost him the respect of the rest. On the day he lands he is thirty-four and can barely manage the language.
sources: International Erich Fromm Society chronology, fromm-online.org/en/life/important-dates/
suggested_refs: The Institute for Social Research in exile at 429 West 117th Street, Morningside Heights

stops.name: Manhattan, the circle outside the Institute
stops.date_confidence: attested for the association by English Wikipedia, which names Horney, Sullivan and Thompson as Fromm's New York circle; the year is an ordering device, the friendships having formed across the later 1930s rather than on a datable day.
stops.campa: He builds a clinical practice in Manhattan and finds, outside the Institute, the company that actually changes his thinking: Karen Horney, Harry Stack Sullivan, Clara Thompson. They meet in an informal seminar the group calls the Zodiac Club. All of them are revising Freud in the same direction, away from the biology of the drives and toward what happens between people and what a culture does to them. The American branch of psychoanalysis that gets called interpersonal begins in these rooms. Fromm and Horney are close for years. They break badly in 1943.
sources: International Erich Fromm Society chronology, fromm-online.org/en/life/important-dates/
suggested_refs: The Zodiac Club, the informal New York seminar of Horney, Sullivan, Thompson and Fromm

stops.name: Morningside Heights, the collective volume and the break
stops.date_confidence: 1936 attested for Studien ueber Autoritaet und Familie by the Institute's own bibliographic record. The break is [R]: reconstructed from Neil McLaughlin's work on Fromm and the Frankfurt School, conventionally dated 1938-39, with sources differing on whether a single decisive break occurred or a gradual estrangement. No single act fixes it. Pin inherited byte-identical from felix_weil.journey.json.
stops.campa: He writes the social-psychological section of Studien ueber Autoritaet und Familie, the collective volume the exiled Institute publishes in 1936, and supplies the survey material behind it. Three years later he is off the payroll. The quarrel is theoretical, over his revision of Freud's theory of the drives, and it is also about money and temperament, and the sources cannot agree whether there was one break or a long cooling. The result is not in dispute. The school later named for Frankfurt tells its origin story without him in it.
sources: Institute for Social Research bibliographic record, via fromm-online.org/en/works/
Neil McLaughlin, 'Origin Myths in the Social Sciences: Fromm, the Frankfurt School and the Emergence of Critical Theory'
suggested_refs: Studien ueber Autoritaet und Familie, Paris, Librairie Felix Alcan, 1936

segments.name: Escape from Freedom: The American Books

stops.name: New York, Escape from Freedom and a new passport
stops.date_confidence: 1941 attested for the book and, per the Fromm Society chronology, for the start of his New School teaching. Naturalization is contradicted between sources and both years are printed: the Fromm Society gives 25 May 1940, the NYPL finding aid gives 1941. English Wikipedia dates the New School association 1941-1959.
stops.campa: Escape from Freedom appears in English, written for readers who have never heard of the Zeitschrift. Its argument is that the freedom won from the medieval order left the individual alone with it, and that the loneliness is unbearable enough that people will hand the freedom back: to a leader, to conformity, to an automaton life that still feels chosen. The British edition is called The Fear of Freedom. He begins teaching at the New School in the same year, and takes American citizenship, in 1940 by one record and 1941 by another.
stops.quote: The kind of relatedness to the world may be noble or trivial, but even being related to the basest kind of pattern is immensely preferable to being alone.
stops.quote_source: Erich Fromm, Escape from Freedom (1941), Ch. 1, via Wikiquote's sourced-quotations compilation
sources: International Erich Fromm Society chronology, fromm-online.org/en/life/important-dates/
suggested_refs: Escape from Freedom, New York, Farrar and Rinehart, 1941; British edition The Fear of Freedom, 1942

stops.name: Bennington, the college in the Vermont hills
stops.date_confidence: contested and printed as such. The Fromm Society chronology reads 1942, accepted a part-time professorship at Bennington College in Vermont; English Wikipedia gives 1941-1949. The file follows the chronology's 1942 and records the disagreement. Coordinates corrected: English Wikipedia gives the college as 42.924817, -73.23673, some 3.2 km north of the research pool's pin, which fell in the town.
stops.campa: He accepts a part-time professorship at Bennington College, an experimental women's college in the Vermont hills where the students build their own courses of study. He keeps the appointment through the decade while living in New York. What Bennington gives him is a room full of undergraduates rather than analysts, and the habit of plain speech that later sells his books by the million. His own chronology dates the start to 1942; English Wikipedia has him there from 1941. Nothing reached settles the disagreement.
stops.quote: ...there is only one meaning of life: the act of living itself.
stops.quote_source: Erich Fromm, Escape from Freedom (1941), Ch. 7, pp. 262-63; the closing clause of a longer sentence, verified against Open Library search-inside and quoted here as the fragment it is
sources: International Erich Fromm Society chronology, fromm-online.org/en/life/important-dates/
suggested_refs: Bennington College's Plan process, under which each student designs her own course of study

stops.name: New York, the William Alanson White Institute
stops.date_confidence: 1943, after a correction. The research pool asserted 1946 on the strength of the dossier; the verification pass found the current English Wikipedia article on the institute gives 1943 and names Fromm and Clara Thompson as founders, joined by Sullivan, Fromm-Reichmann and David and Janet Rioch, agreeing with the Fromm Society chronology. 1946 may be the year a New York branch took the White name; no fetched source documents that and it is not asserted. The institute has held more than one Manhattan address; the pin is city precision.
stops.campa: A lay analyst holding a doctorate in sociology and no medical degree cannot be trained or certified by the American establishment, so the establishment is bypassed. With Clara Thompson he founds a training institute of their own, joined by Harry Stack Sullivan, Frieda Fromm-Reichmann, and David and Janet Rioch, and they give it the name of William Alanson White. It will train whoever it judges fit to be trained, degree or no degree. He breaks with Karen Horney the same year.
sources: International Erich Fromm Society chronology, fromm-online.org/en/life/important-dates/
suggested_refs: The William Alanson White Institute of Psychiatry, Psychoanalysis and Psychology, New York, founded 1943

stops.name: New York, the marriage to Henny Gurland
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by the Fromm Society chronology and English Wikipedia. Her presence in the Pyrenees party of September 1940 is carried by the same sources; the pin is New York at city precision, no venue being recorded.
stops.campa: On the twenty-fourth of July he marries Henny Gurland, born Henny Meyer, a photographer who came over the Pyrenees in September 1940 in the small party that crossed with Walter Benjamin to Portbou, where Benjamin died. She arrives in the marriage with an illness that never leaves her. Fromm spends the next eight years arranging his life around her pain, and in the end it is her body, not his career, that decides where he lives. What she saw on that crossing she does not much discuss, and no account of it in her own words has been found.
sources: International Erich Fromm Society chronology, fromm-online.org/en/life/important-dates/
suggested_refs: The Lister route over the Pyrenees from Banyuls to Portbou, September 1940

stops.name: New York, Man for Himself and the marketing character
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year by the Fromm Institute works database. The pin is the New School, where he was teaching in these years; no source records where the book was written, and the coordinate should be read as a working location and not a composition site.
stops.campa: Man for Himself lays out a typology of character that outlives most of its rivals: receptive, exploitative, hoarding, marketing, productive. Fromm writes it as an ethics, on the ground that psychoanalysis has no business pretending to be free of values. The marketing orientation is the new type and the one that lands. A man who experiences himself as a commodity, whose worth is his price on a market of personalities, feels his value rise and fall with the demand for him and cannot say what is wrong with him.
stops.quote: Man is the only animal for whom his own existence is a problem which he has to solve and from which he cannot escape.
stops.quote_source: Erich Fromm, Man for Himself (1947), Ch. 3, via Wikiquote's sourced-quotations compilation
sources: Erich Fromm Institute works database, fromm-online.org/en/works/
suggested_refs: Man for Himself: An Inquiry into the Psychology of Ethics, New York, Rinehart, 1947

stops.name: New Haven, the Terry Lectures
stops.date_confidence: contested and printed as such. The NYPL finding aid and Yale's own roll of Terry Lecturers give 1949-50; the Fromm Society chronology gives 1948 for the lectures themselves. The book followed in 1950. Pin tightened to the Yale campus centre from the research pool's coordinate, which sat some 800 m southwest.
stops.campa: Yale invites him to give the Terry Lectures, endowed for religion considered in the light of science and philosophy, and he uses them to cut religion in two. Authoritarian religion asks for surrender to a power outside the self. Humanistic religion asks for the unfolding of what is inside it. Both have gone under one name for three thousand years, and Fromm argues that an analyst who cannot tell them apart will mistake a man's submission for his faith. The lectures appear in 1950 as Psychoanalysis and Religion.
sources: International Erich Fromm Society chronology, fromm-online.org/en/life/important-dates/
suggested_refs: Psychoanalysis and Religion, Yale University Press, 1950, the Dwight Harrington Terry Foundation Lectures

stops.name: Mexico City, the move made for a wife
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by the Fromm Society chronology, which also gives the reason as Henny Gurland's health; English Wikipedia dates a first visit to 1949.
stops.campa: On the sixth of June he arrives in Mexico City with Henny. The move is made for her: the altitude and the sulphur springs are supposed to reach what the American doctors cannot. He is fifty and at the height of an American reputation, and he leaves it for a country where he must learn a third language and build a practice from nothing. He never lives in the United States again, though he keeps flying north to teach in it for another fifteen years. The Mexican years will run to twenty-four.
sources: International Erich Fromm Society chronology, fromm-online.org/en/life/important-dates/
suggested_refs: The sulphur springs of Morelos, the reason given in the family record for the Mexican move

stops.name: Ciudad Universitaria, the medical faculty of UNAM
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year by the Fromm Society chronology, the NYPL finding aid and English Wikipedia; no month recorded. The Forgotten Language is dated 1951 by the works database.
stops.campa: The National Autonomous University makes him professor in the faculty of medicine, and there he does what New York would not let him do: train analysts from the beginning, in Spanish, in a country with almost no psychoanalytic tradition to argue against. The Forgotten Language comes out the same year, on dreams and myths as one symbolic tongue that every culture has spoken and every modern adult has lost the ability to read. The training group he forms becomes the Sociedad Psicoanalitica Mexicana.
sources: International Erich Fromm Society chronology, fromm-online.org/en/life/important-dates/
suggested_refs: The Sociedad Psicoanalitica Mexicana, grown from Fromm's UNAM training group

stops.name: Mexico City, the death of Henny Gurland Fromm
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by the Fromm Society chronology and English Wikipedia. Nothing of the funeral or burial is recorded in any source reached; the pin is Mexico City at city precision.
stops.campa: Henny Gurland Fromm dies on the fourth of June, two years after the move made on her account. She had survived the crossing of the Pyrenees, the death of Benjamin at Portbou, the refugee years and the American exile, and the country she was brought to for her health did not cure her. The marriage had lasted eight years, most of them inside her illness. Fromm is fifty-two and alone in a city he came to for a woman who is no longer in it. He does not go back north. He goes on teaching through the year.
sources: International Erich Fromm Society chronology, fromm-online.org/en/life/important-dates/
suggested_refs: Henny Gurland's photographic work, largely unrecovered, made in Germany and in exile before 1940

stops.name: Mexico City, the marriage to Annis Freeman
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by the Fromm Society chronology and English Wikipedia, which give her as Annis Freeman, nee Glover, born in Alabama.
stops.campa: On the eighteenth of December he marries Annis Freeman, born Annis Glover in Alabama, a woman with no professional stake in psychoanalysis and no patience for its vocabulary. He is fifty-three and has been married twice already, once to his own analyst and once to a woman he nursed for eight years. The Art of Loving, which argues that love is a practice requiring discipline, patience and concentration, is written three years into this one. The marriage runs twenty-seven years and ends on the day he dies.
stops.quote: Immature love says: 'I love you because I need you.' Mature love says: 'I need you because I love you.'
stops.quote_source: Erich Fromm, The Art of Loving (1956), Ch. 2, via Wikiquote's sourced-quotations compilation
sources: International Erich Fromm Society chronology, fromm-online.org/en/life/important-dates/
suggested_refs: Annis Freeman Fromm, the third marriage, 1953 to 1980

stops.name: Mexico City, The Sane Society
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year by the Fromm Institute works database, which also dates Marcuse's Eros and Civilization to 1955. Note a correction carried out of the research pool: Fromm did not found SANE. English Wikipedia gives the National Committee for a Sane Nuclear Policy as founded in November 1957 by Lenore Marshall and Norman Cousins, and states that the name came from the concepts in Fromm's book.
stops.campa: The Sane Society asks a question the discipline had ruled out of order: whether a whole society can be sick. If mental health is measured by adjustment to the society one lives in, then a society built on alienated work and consumption turns out adjusted men who are ill, and the therapist who returns them to it is running a repair shop. Two years later an American committee against nuclear testing takes its name, SANE, from this book. Herbert Marcuse answers it the same year in Eros and Civilization, calling Fromm a revisionist who has softened Freud into a preacher.
stops.quote: Just as modern mass production requires the standardization of commodities, so the social process requires standardization of man, and this standardization is called equality.
stops.quote_source: Erich Fromm, The Art of Loving (1956), Ch. 2, p. 16; verified against Open Library search-inside, which shows the clause the common shortened version drops
sources: Erich Fromm Institute works database, fromm-online.org/en/works/
suggested_refs: Herbert Marcuse, Eros and Civilization (1955), epilogue on neo-Freudian revisionism

stops.name: Cuernavaca, the house and The Art of Loving
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of the move and the book by the Fromm Society chronology; no month recorded and no address confirmed, so the pin is Cuernavaca at city precision. The sales figure of over 1.5 million English-language copies by 1970 is Rainer Funk's, a house source.
stops.campa: He and Annis come down from the capital to Cuernavaca in Morelos and build a house with a garden, where the air is warm all year and the work goes better. The Art of Loving is published the same year. Its argument is unfashionable and plain: love is not a feeling that happens to a person but an art with a theory and a practice, and a civilisation that treats it as luck will go on failing at it. Rainer Funk, his executor, puts the English sales past a million and a half copies by 1970.
stops.quote: If it is true, as I have tried to show, that love is the only sane and satisfactory answer to the problem of human existence, then any society which excludes, relatively, the development of love, must in the long run perish of its own contradiction with the basic necessities of human nature.
stops.quote_source: Erich Fromm, The Art of Loving (1956); full text restored from Open Library search-inside, the widely circulated version having dropped the middle clause and cut the sentence at perish. Wikiquote gives no chapter and the passage is not in Ch. 2
sources: International Erich Fromm Society chronology, fromm-online.org/en/life/important-dates/
suggested_refs: The Art of Loving in at least twenty-one languages, from Arabic to Ukrainian

stops.name: Cuernavaca, the Zen seminar with Suzuki
stops.date_confidence: [R]. The Fromm Society chronology places the Zen seminars with D. T. Suzuki at Cuernavaca in 1957 and the book in 1960; the research pass could not independently confirm the Cuernavaca venue. Frieda Fromm-Reichmann's death is dated 1957 by the same chronology. Cited here rather than staged: elsa_gindler.journey.json names Fromm among the figures crossing Charlotte Selver's path as Sensory Awareness reaches America at Esalen in 1963, but nothing in the record reached places Fromm on that coast, so no Esalen stop is made.
stops.campa: He brings D. T. Suzuki to Cuernavaca and convenes a week of seminars on Zen and psychoanalysis, with Richard de Martino and a room of analysts. What Fromm takes from it is a confirmation rather than a conversion: that the aim of analysis is not adjustment but a waking up, an attention that does not grasp at what it sees. Frieda Fromm-Reichmann dies in the same year, thirty-three years after the Heidelberg house where patients were analysed in the morning and kept the dietary laws at table. The papers appear in 1960 as Zen Buddhism and Psychoanalysis.
stops.quote: Care and responsibility are constituent elements of love, but without respect for and knowledge of the beloved person, love deteriorates into domination and possessiveness.
stops.quote_source: Erich Fromm, Man for Himself (1947), Ch. 3, verified verbatim against Open Library search-inside; the same formulation recurs in The Art of Loving, Ch. 2
sources: International Erich Fromm Society chronology, fromm-online.org/en/life/important-dates/
suggested_refs: Zen Buddhism and Psychoanalysis, with D. T. Suzuki and Richard de Martino, 1960
elsa_gindler.journey.json, Esalen 1963, which names Fromm among those crossing Charlotte Selver's path

stops.name: East Lansing, the chair at Michigan State
stops.date_confidence: attested for the years 1957-1961 by English Wikipedia and the NYPL finding aid; no month recorded, and June is set here only to order the segment after the Cuernavaca seminar. The 1958 Mike Wallace television interview falls inside this period; the broadcast is attested but no source reached records a studio or city, so it is cited here rather than given a stop of its own.
stops.campa: He takes a professorship in psychology at Michigan State and holds it four years, flying up from Mexico to teach in a land-grant university in the flat middle of a country he has stopped living in. These are the years of the campus paperback, and Fromm is on the racks in every drugstore: a European analyst explaining American loneliness to Americans in sentences they can read standing up. The professional journals cool as the print runs climb. In 1958 Mike Wallace puts him on television for half an hour and asks him about love, conformity and the republic.
suggested_refs: The Mike Wallace Interview with Erich Fromm, 1958, held in the Harry Ransom Center's Wallace collection

stops.name: Cuernavaca, Sigmund Freud's Mission
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year by the Fromm Institute works database; the death of Rosa Fromm in New York is dated 1959 by the Fromm Society chronology. No month recorded for either. The pin is his own house at Cuernavaca; his mother died in New York and that is her stop, not his.
stops.campa: He publishes Sigmund Freud's Mission, an analysis of the personality of the man who founded the discipline: Freud as a Victorian patriarch whose theory of the drives carries the marks of his own authoritarianism, and whose greatness cannot be separated from that limit. It is the second of three books Fromm writes about Freud across his life. He is fifty-nine, and both of his fathers, the one who sold wine and the one who wrote the dream book, have become subjects rather than authorities. Rosa Fromm dies in New York the same year, the last of the Frankfurt household.
sources: Erich Fromm Institute works database, fromm-online.org/en/works/
International Erich Fromm Society chronology, fromm-online.org/en/life/important-dates/
suggested_refs: Sigmund Freud's Mission: An Analysis of His Personality and Influence, 1959

stops.name: The villages of Morelos, the social character measured
stops.date_confidence: [R] as to the site. English Wikipedia's article on Michael Maccoby confirms that Maccoby lived in Mexico from 1960 to 1968 working with Fromm, and that the study appeared as Social Character in a Mexican Village in 1970. The village is not named there, in Maccoby's own entry, or anywhere else reached, so the pin is rural Morelos at approximate precision and the gap is stated in the campa.
stops.campa: With Michael Maccoby he begins eight years of fieldwork in a village in the state of Morelos, interviewing every adult in the place with questionnaires, Rorschach cards and dream reports, to find out whether social character can be measured rather than merely asserted. The results, published in 1970, sort the villagers into productive, hoarding and receptive types and set them against land tenure and drink. Which village it was is not named in anything reachable, not even by Maccoby.
sources: Erich Fromm and Michael Maccoby, Social Character in a Mexican Village (Prentice-Hall, 1970)
suggested_refs: Social Character in a Mexican Village: A Sociopsychoanalytic Study, 1970

stops.name: Cuernavaca, Marx read as a humanist
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of both books by the Fromm Institute works database; no month recorded. The pin is his own house, no composition site being documented.
stops.campa: He publishes May Man Prevail?, which reads the Cold War as a shared delusion in which each side hallucinates the other's intentions, arms itself accordingly, and then points at the armament as proof. The same year he publishes Marx's Concept of Man, printing the 1844 Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts in English with a long introduction and arguing that Karl Marx was a humanist whose subject was alienation, not a determinist whose subject was economics. Saying that out loud in the United States in 1961 costs something.
sources: Erich Fromm Institute works database, fromm-online.org/en/works/
suggested_refs: Marx's Concept of Man, with the 1844 Manuscripts translated by T. B. Bottomore, 1961
The New York University adjunct professorship in psychology, held from 1962 after the Michigan State years ended, per the NYPL finding aid

segments.name: Biophilia and Necrophilia: The Late Politics

stops.name: Cuernavaca, The Heart of Man
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year by the Fromm Institute works database; no month recorded. The quotation attached is from Credo (1965), a year later than the book, and states the same distinction in Fromm's own compressed form.
stops.campa: The Heart of Man sets out the spectrum he works with for the rest of his life. Biophilia is the love of what lives, grows and is uncertain. Necrophilia is the attraction to what is dead, mechanical and in order. He is not naming a diagnosis but a direction a character can face, and he holds that most people face both ways and that societies can tip the balance. He has been arguing publicly against the arms race since the fifties, and he thinks the men running it are in love with the machinery. He states the distinction again a year later, in his own most compressed form, in the Credo.
stops.quote: By necrophilia is meant love for all that is violence and destruction; the desire to kill; the worship of force; attraction to death, to suicide, to sadism; the desire to transform the organic into the inorganic by means of 'order.'
stops.quote_source: Erich Fromm, Credo (1965), first published in English in On Being Human, ed. Rainer Funk (1994), pp. 99-105; full sentence restored from Open Library search-inside
sources: Erich Fromm Institute works database, fromm-online.org/en/works/
suggested_refs: The Heart of Man: Its Genius for Good and Evil, 1964

stops.name: Ciudad Universitaria, retirement from UNAM
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year by the Fromm Society chronology and English Wikipedia; no month recorded. Socialist Humanism is dated 1965 by the same sources.
stops.campa: He retires from the medical faculty at sixty-five, after fourteen years spent building a psychoanalytic training in a country that had none, and the institute he founded goes on without him. In the same year he edits Socialist Humanism, a symposium on whether socialism can still be argued about as a moral proposition rather than a form of state. Yugoslav and Polish Marxists write in it alongside Western ones, contributors from both sides of the Iron Curtain bound into one volume, in 1965.
sources: International Erich Fromm Society chronology, fromm-online.org/en/life/important-dates/
suggested_refs: Socialist Humanism: An International Symposium, edited by Erich Fromm, 1965

stops.name: Cuernavaca, the prophets and the first heart attack
stops.date_confidence: attested. The Fromm Society chronology dates the heart attack to 6 December 1966 and places the book and the American Humanist Association award in the same year; the book and the award have no recorded day.
stops.campa: You Shall Be as Gods reads the Hebrew Bible as the record of a people arguing with its own God, moving from a tribal deity who bargains to a nameless X that no image can hold, and reads the prophets as a political tradition rather than a devotional one. The book comes straight out of the Talmud afternoons in Heidelberg forty years earlier. The American Humanist Association names him Humanist of the Year. On the sixth of December, at sixty-six, he has his first heart attack.
sources: International Erich Fromm Society chronology, fromm-online.org/en/life/important-dates/
suggested_refs: You Shall Be as Gods: A Radical Interpretation of the Old Testament and Its Tradition, 1966

stops.name: Cuernavaca, hope and the McCarthy campaign
stops.date_confidence: 1968 attested for the book by the works database and for the McCarthy campaign work by the same record. Flagged: no source reached says whether that work was done in the United States or from Mexico by correspondence, and the campa now states that gap rather than inferring a location from his residence.
stops.campa: He writes The Revolution of Hope: Toward a Humanized Technology, arguing that a technical system will keep producing whatever it is capable of producing unless human ends are set in front of it deliberately, and that hope is not optimism but readiness. In the same year he works for Eugene McCarthy's campaign against the war, drafting position papers and speech material for a candidate running to end it. He is sixty-eight and two years past a heart attack. Whether he did that work in the United States or by post from his desk in Morelos is not recorded.
stops.quote: To hope means to be ready at every moment for that which is not yet born, and yet not become desperate if there is no birth in our lifetime.
stops.quote_source: Erich Fromm, The Revolution of Hope (1968), via Wikiquote's sourced-quotations compilation
sources: Erich Fromm Institute works database, fromm-online.org/en/works/
suggested_refs: Fromm's drafts for the Eugene McCarthy presidential campaign, 1968, Erich Fromm papers, NYPL

stops.name: Locarno, an apartment rented for the summers
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year by the Fromm Society chronology: rented Locarno apartment in Tessin, Switzerland, for summers. No month, no address. The pin is Locarno town; the later permanent residence at Muralto is pinned separately.
stops.campa: He rents an apartment in Locarno, on the Swiss side of the lake in the Ticino, for the summers. The reasons are medical and practical at once: European doctors, European publishers, and a climate his heart tolerates better than the altitude of Morelos. After thirty years of writing English for Americans, he is writing German again, for Germans, in an Italian-speaking canton. For five years he keeps both houses and crosses the Atlantic twice a year.
sources: International Erich Fromm Society chronology, fromm-online.org/en/life/important-dates/
suggested_refs: The Ticino colony of German-speaking exiles and returnees around Locarno and Ascona

stops.name: Cuernavaca, The Anatomy of Human Destructiveness
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year by the Fromm Institute works database; no month recorded. The pin is Cuernavaca, where he was still resident in 1973, the permanent move to Switzerland falling in 1974.
stops.campa: After years of reading in animal behaviour, palaeontology and the neurology of aggression, he publishes The Anatomy of Human Destructiveness against the instinct theorists. Aggression that defends life is common to the animals and is not the problem. The cruelty that takes pleasure in destroying is human, historical, produced by conditions, and therefore alterable, which is the whole point of insisting on the distinction. The book closes with clinical portraits of Himmler, Stalin and Hitler as necrophilous characters.
stops.quote: Optimism is an alienated form of faith, pessimism an alienated form of despair.
stops.quote_source: Erich Fromm, The Anatomy of Human Destructiveness (1973), p. 483, via Wikiquote's sourced-quotations compilation
sources: Erich Fromm Institute works database, fromm-online.org/en/works/
suggested_refs: The Anatomy of Human Destructiveness, New York, Holt, Rinehart and Winston, 1973

segments.name: Muralto: To Have or To Be

stops.name: Muralto, the last address
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year by the Fromm Society chronology: abandoned Cuernavaca residence for year-round Tessin living. Coordinates corrected to those given by English Wikipedia for Muralto, the research pool having carried three different wrong values. The Senate submission is [R], a dossier lead not independently confirmed and probably written rather than delivered in person; no Washington stop is staged for it.
stops.campa: At seventy-four he gives up the Cuernavaca house and moves to Muralto, on the lake below Locarno, for good. Annis comes with him. His heart will not take the flying any more, and the twenty-four Mexican years are closed. In the same year he sends written remarks on the policy of detente to the Foreign Relations Committee of the United States Senate, arguing against the reading of Soviet intentions on which the whole apparatus of the arms race rests. Whether he crossed the Atlantic to say it is not recorded.
sources: International Erich Fromm Society chronology, fromm-online.org/en/life/important-dates/
suggested_refs: Remarks on the Policy of Detente, submitted to the US Senate Committee on Foreign Relations, 1974

stops.name: Muralto, To Have or To Be
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of the book by the Fromm Institute works database. A correction is carried here out of the research pool, which had placed a third heart attack in 1976 and printed the entry out of sequence: the Fromm Society chronology gives gallbladder surgery in New York in 1975, a second heart attack in 1977 and a third in 1978, and no heart attack at all in 1976.
stops.campa: To Have or To Be? divides every human activity in two according to the verb behind it. To have is to hold a thing, a person or an idea as property, and to be diminished when it goes. To be is to exercise a capacity, which no one can lose by using it. He writes it in the year after gallbladder surgery in New York, and it is the last of his books to sell in the millions. It ends with the sketch of a society organised on the second verb, which he does not expect to see. A second heart attack follows in 1977 and a third in 1978.
sources: Erich Fromm Institute works database, fromm-online.org/en/works/
International Erich Fromm Society chronology, fromm-online.org/en/life/important-dates/
suggested_refs: To Have or To Be?, New York, Harper and Row, 1976

stops.name: Dortmund, the Nelly Sachs Prize
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year and the awarding city by English Wikipedia, 'Nelly Sachs Prize', which lists Fromm as the 1979 recipient. No source reached states whether Fromm travelled to Dortmund to receive it, and the campa says so rather than staging an attendance.
stops.campa: The city of Dortmund awards him the Nelly Sachs Prize, named for the German-Jewish poet who wrote the elegies of the destroyed. Germany is honouring, at the end of his life, a Frankfurt Jew it expelled at thirty-four. It is the last public honour he receives. In the same year the German original of his last book on Freud is published. He is seventy-nine and has survived three heart attacks; whether he crossed the Alps to stand up and accept the prize in person is not recorded in anything reachable.
sources: Erich Fromm Institute works database, fromm-online.org/en/works/
suggested_refs: The Nelly Sachs Prize of the city of Dortmund, awarded biennially since 1961

stops.name: Muralto, death five days short of eighty
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by the Fromm Society chronology, English Wikipedia and German Wikipedia. The chronology specifies a fourth heart attack, a detail the standard summaries drop. On the last book: the German original, Sigmund Freuds Psychoanalyse, Groesse und Grenzen, is 1979; the English edition is 1980, the year of his death. The Gesamtausgabe volume count is contradicted, ten volumes per German Wikipedia's death sentence against twelve completed by 1999 in the same article and per the Fromm Institute; both are printed and neither adopted.
stops.campa: He dies at home in Muralto on the eighteenth of March, of a fourth heart attack, five days before his eightieth birthday. Annis is with him. His last book, on the greatness and the limits of Freud's thought, had come out in German the year before and appears in English in the year of his death, so that the argument he began as a training analyst in Berlin in 1928 and never finished is still on the presses when he stops. The German collected edition is in press and he does not see it. Sixty million copies of his books have been sold.
sources: International Erich Fromm Society chronology, fromm-online.org/en/life/important-dates/
Erich Fromm Study Center, IPU Berlin, efsc.ipu-berlin.de/en/erich-fromm
suggested_refs: The Greatness and Limitations of Freud's Thought, German 1979, English 1980
The Erich Fromm Gesamtausgabe, edited by Rainer Funk, Deutsche Verlags-Anstalt

stops.name: Bellinzona, the cremation
stops.date_confidence: attested as to place and rite, undated as to day. German Wikipedia states verbatim: Erich Fromm wurde in Bellinzona (Schweiz) beigesetzt. The Fromm Society chronology says outright that he was cremated in Bellinzona, which closes the question the German verb leaves open. No source reached names the cemetery. The date is set to the day of death only to hold the segment in order; the actual date of the cremation is not recorded. Coordinates corrected to those given by English Wikipedia for Bellinzona.
stops.campa: His body is taken up the valley to Bellinzona and cremated. The German record says only that he was laid to rest there; his own society's chronology says cremated; the cemetery is named by neither. He had left Frankfurt in 1934, the United States in 1950 and Mexico in 1974, and he ends in the Italian-speaking canton of the country he first entered in 1931 to be cured of tuberculosis. The papers go to the New York Public Library. The library, the estate and the unpublished manuscripts go to Tuebingen.
sources: International Erich Fromm Society chronology, fromm-online.org/en/life/important-dates/
